payload.name: silicon (diamond cubic)
payload.structure_source: ideal diamond-cubic Fd-3m prototype (ase.build.bulk, cubic 8-atom cell); cf. Materials Project mp-149
payload.rationale: Requested system: EOS lattice constant of diamond-cubic Si.

_fulfilled_need.query: Compute the equilibrium lattice constant of diamond-cubic silicon from an equation-of-state fit.

summary: candidate silicon (diamond cubic) (elemental semiconductor, trust tier)

method.engine: ASE 3.29 + mace-torch 0.3.15 (ALCHEMI toolkit environment, GPU, float64)
method.protocol: Static (0 K, no zero-point/thermal) energy-volume scan of the 8-atom cubic diamond cell, 3rd-order Birch-Murnaghan fit over a0*(1+/-5%) with 15 points; cross-checked with Vinet and Murnaghan forms over +/-3%, 5%, 8% windows, and with a hydrostatic cell relaxation (ExpCellFilter+BFGS, fmax 1e-5). Pressure from model stress at fitted a = 0.0000 GPa. E/atom identical for 1x1x1, 2x2x2, 3x3x3 supercells (8/64/216 atoms).

payload.note: Uncertainty (+/-0.006 A) covers numerical EOS fit form/window spread (5.4654-5.4672 A), agreement between EOS fit and stress-based relaxation (5.4674 A), and the model's deviation from its PBE reference for Si (MACE 5.466 vs PBE 5.472 A). It does NOT cover the systematic error of the PBE functional relative to experiment: the result is a static-lattice PBE-quality value and is ~0.65% above the measured CODATA lattice parameter 5.431020511(89) A at 22.5 C (NIST CODATA 2018 X-ray table), and ~0.8% above a zero-point-corrected experimental value (~5.421 A, as tabulated in arXiv:2601.11177). Zero-point and thermal expansion are not included (static calculation). Validation (same model/protocol): MACE-MPA-0 vs literature PBE: Si 5.466 vs 5.472, Al 4.037 vs 4.042, Cu 3.639 vs 3.642, C 3.578 vs 3.571, Ge 5.720 vs 5.765 (PBE values as tabulated in arXiv:2601.11177 and arXiv:2604.07046, retrieved via web search). Bulk modulus 88.4 GPa. Si is in the MACE-MPA-0 training domain (MPtrj/sAlex PBE data), so the Si-vs-PBE comparison is not fully independent; Al/Cu/C give out-of-sample confirmation of the protocol. The tier1 calibration file contains no lattice-constant records, so it was not used.

summary: silicon (diamond cubic) lattice_constant = 5.466 angstrom via ASE 3.29 + mace-torch 0.3.15 (ALCHEMI toolkit environment, GPU, float64)/MACE-MPA-0 (medium) Static (0 K, no zero-point/thermal) energy-volume scan of the 8-atom cubic diamond cell, 3rd-order Birch-Murnaghan fit over a0*(1+/-5%) with 15 points; cross-checked with Vinet and Murnaghan forms over +/-3%, 5%, 8% windows, and with a hydrostatic cell relaxation (ExpCellFilter+BFGS, fmax 1e-5). Pressure from model stress at fitted a = 0.0000 GPa. E/atom identical for 1x1x1, 2x2x2, 3x3x3 supercells (8/64/216 atoms).

payload.note: Same MACE-MPA-0 static EOS protocol recovers literature PBE lattice constants for Al (4.037 vs 4.042 A), Cu (3.639 vs 3.642), C (3.578 vs 3.571), Si (5.466 vs 5.472) within 0.2%; Ge low by 0.8% (5.720 vs 5.765) (PBE values as tabulated in arXiv:2601.11177 and arXiv:2604.07046). Against experiment the result shows the expected PBE overestimate (Si +0.65% vs CODATA 5.431020511(89) A at 22.5 C, NIST CODATA 2018 X-ray table). Supercell test (8/64/216 atoms) gives identical E/atom; model stress at fitted a is zero.

Static 0 K lattice constant of a perfect diamond-cubic crystal is well defined for an MLIP EOS fit: no timescale/sampling issue, periodic 8-atom cell is exact for a perfect crystal (energy per atom verified identical up to 216 atoms), and Si is inside the MACE-MPA-0 (PBE-trained) domain. Limitation: result inherits PBE bias and excludes zero-point/thermal expansion, so it is a PBE-level static value, not a direct room-temperature prediction.
